title: Reliability Workbench: Deployment Cadence & Steward Protocol
content:
Purpose:
This document captures a pragmatic cross-functional plan for operationalizing SLOs and running a recurring deployment cadence using a lightweight "reliability workbench". The workbench is a set of conventions, templates, and a short sprint pattern teams can adopt to move from SLO definition -> measurement -> runbook -> stewarded rollout in ~90 days.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: model-serving services (hosted API + dedicated capacity) and associated control plane components that carry customer-facing latency and availability guarantees.
- Audience: feature-team leads, SRE stewards, product managers (hosted/dedicated), observability engineers, platform oncall owners, and solutions eng.

Principles:
1) Minimal friction: handoffs should be just-in-time and template-driven so feature teams can adopt the workbench without heavy consulting.
2) Measurable early: start with concrete telemetry (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, throughput, traffic-weighted availability) and SLO targets that map to customer impact.
3) Incremental rollout: validate in canary -> regional -> global stages with rollback hooks and fallbacks.
4) Clear stewards: each SLO has an assigned steward who owns monitoring thresholds, runbooks, and postmortems.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Feature Team Lead: defines customer impact and initial SLO target; implements metrics and tagging.
- SRE Steward: validates metrics, owns alert thresholds, runbook authoring, and oncall escalation chain.
- Observability Eng: ensures dashboards and dashboards-as-code templates are available; maintains query performance.
- Platform Ops: coordinates deployment windows and capacity planning for Dedicated pools.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: flags customers who should be included in canary cohorts or notified during rollouts.

90-Day Workbench Sprint Pattern (4 two-week sprints):
Sprint 0 (prep, week 0-2):
- Kickoff: define customer journey and the critical path (3–5 user flows).
- Baseline telemetry: capture current p50/p95 latency, error-rate and request-volume histograms.
- Fill the runbook template (initial sections) and identify missing instrumentation.
Deliverables: SLO spec doc, baseline dashboard, runbook draft.

Sprint 1 (measure & alert, week 3-4):
- Implement or refine metrics (service-level metrics, latency bucketing, traffic labels).
- Create SLO dashboard + burn rate queries.
- Define and configure alerts (burn-rate + immediate symptom alerts).
Deliverables: Observability-as-code PR, alert rules merged to staging.

Sprint 2 (resilience & runbook, week 5-6):
- Run tabletop: simulated incidents using the runbook; capture gaps.
- Add fallback/circuit-breaker config and test in canary environment.
- Finalize runbook steps for mitigation, escalation, and postmortem template.
Deliverables: Runbook v1, canary test report, updated mitigation configs.

Sprint 3 (rollout & handoff, week 7-10):
- Gradual rollout plan executed (10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic) with guardrails.
- Observe burn-rate and circuit breakers; execute rollback if needed.
- Handoff: SRE steward takes ownership for ongoing operational support and quarterly reviews.
Deliverables: Rollout report, steward acceptance signoff, retros/lessons learned.

Operational artifacts (templates) included in the workbench:
- SLO spec (1-pager): objective, metrics, measurement window, and customer impact section.
- Runbook template: symptoms, immediate mitigation, escalation, triage checklist, owner contact, follow-up actions.
- Rollout checklist: preflight queries, safety checks, canary gating thresholds, communication plan.
- Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause hypotheses, corrective actions, verification plan.

Telemetry and measurement guidance:
- Use traffic-weighted SLO calculations for mixed-priority customers.
- Prefer 30-day rolling windows for availability and a 7-day window for short-term burn-rate alerts.
- Record both absolute counts and ratios in dashboards to avoid alert storms during volume spikes.

Communication & stakeholder cadence:
- Weekly triage sync (15m) during Sprint 1-2 to unblock instrumentation and alerts.
- Deployment day channel: #rwb-rollouts (Slack) with pinned preflight checklist and status updates.
- Steering review at the end of Sprint 3: stakeholders (PM, SRE leads, Platform Ops) sign off steward readiness.

Risk model & contingency plans:
- Capacity risk: prebook Dedicated buffer for rollout windows; Platform Ops to maintain a 20% headroom.
- Telemetry gaps: fallback to synthetic probes and distributed tracing if service metrics are delayed.
- Customer impact: have a customer-cutover rollback plan that can revert traffic routing in <5 minutes.

Oncall & stewardship expectations:
- Steward rotates with a 12-week nominal tenure to ensure continuity but avoids single-person dependency.
- Runbooks must include explicit escalation timelines (0–5m immediate mitigation contact, 5–20m SRE lead, 20–60m oncall rotation escalation).

Success criteria & metrics for adoption (90-day):
- 80% of teams using the SLO spec template for new services or major releases.
- Burn-rate alert cadence reduced by 30% from noisy thresholding (improved signal-to-noise).
- Time-to-detect (TTD) decreases by 25% and time-to-mitigate (TTM) decreases by 20% for incidents related to the targeted SLOs.

Scaling the workbench (post-90 days):
- Create an internal catalog of completed workbench projects with runbook excerpts and key learnings.
- Automate SLO onboarding via a scaffolded repo/template that injects dashboards and alerts for common service patterns.
- Quarterly "stewardship retrofit" where stewards review SLOs for drift and alignment to business SLAs.

Quick reference: common queries and gating thresholds (examples)
- Canary gating: p95 latency increase <= 15% over baseline AND error-rate change <= 0.5% absolute before expanding cohort.
- Burn-rate trigger: 7-day burn-rate > 2x planned safe burn for 3 consecutive evaluation windows.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should dedicated capacity reservations be automatically provisioned for any rollout above 30% traffic? (Platform Ops input needed)
- Policy on customer notifications for partial failovers vs full rollbacks.
- Level of automation for rollback triggers (manual approval vs automated action after gating failure).

Next steps (owner: Maya Chen):
1) Share this doc with feature leads and Platform Ops for feedback by 2026-03-30.
2) Pilot runbench with the "rlm-cache" service in April 2026; schedule kickoff meeting week of 2026-04-04.
3) Build the templates into the observability-as-code repo and open PRs for the canary dashboard and alert rules.

Appendix: useful links and templates
- SLO spec template: CONFLUENCE-9876
- Runbook template: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/blob/main/templates/rwb-runbook.md
- Example rollout playbook (rlm-cache pilot): JIRA-RWB-42

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally opinionated to reduce friction. We expect local tweaks but want consistent guardrails.
- Focus feedback on the steward rotation cadence, canary gating numbers, and Platform Ops capacity policy.
